name: Tourist Entry (CA-4)

requirements.blocker_text: Citizens of roughly 83 countries (US, Canada, UK, EU states, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel) enter without an advance visa and receive an automatic 90-day tourist stamp. Guatemala is part of the CA-4 Border Control Agreement with El Salvador, Honduras, and Nicaragua -- the 90-day allowance is SHARED across all four countries combined, not reset by crossing between them. A single 90-day extension (to 180 days total) is available at IGM for USD 25. After 180 days (or 90 without extension), the traveler must exit the entire CA-4 zone -- only Mexico, Belize, or Costa Rica count as valid reset destinations -- typically for 72+ hours before re-entry.
requirements.fix_path: For non-visa-exempt nationalities, apply for a visa in advance through a Guatemalan consulate.

evidence_required.document: IGM extension application (if extending beyond 90 days)

outcome.duration_length: 90 days (shared CA-4 allowance), extendable once to 180 days

sources.title: Atitlan Vida (private expat-guide site) -- CA-4 shared 90-day allowance, visa-free nationality list, extension process at IGM, and the reset-zone rule (Mexico/Belize/Costa Rica only)

STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a tier-4 private expat-guide site; IGM's own government page on tourist visa policy was not independently fetched in this build (several igm.gob.gt pages returned 403 errors when fetched directly for other routes in this build -- see gt_family_reunification.json's notes). GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE, WELL-DOCUMENTED REGIONAL MECHANISM: the CA-4 Border Control Agreement's SHARED 90-day allowance across four sovereign countries (Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua) is a real, specific structural feature not seen in this exact form elsewhere in this dataset -- a tourist cannot reset the clock by simply crossing to a CA-4 neighbor, only by leaving the whole bloc. duration_type set 'rolling_window' to reflect that the 90/180-day count is a rolling allowance across a shared four-country zone, not a fixed single-country stay.
